{{alias}}( order, uplo, N, KD, AB, LDAB, S, SCOND, AMAX )
    Computes diagonal scaling for a symmetric compact band matrix.
    S[i]=1/sqrt(diagonal[i]), SCOND=sqrt(min)/sqrt(max), AMAX=max.
    Input AB is unchanged. INFO is zero or the first one-based
    nonpositive diagonal. On failure all original diagonals are copied
    to S, AMAX includes later columns and SCOND retains its sentinel.
    Strict-first zero ties differ from sampled reference AMAX failures.

    H=KD+1; full AB is H-by-N. Upper diagonal row KD, lower row zero.
    KD>=N is supported. Selected diagonals must be finite before any
    output write; ignored entries may be nonfinite. Positive diagonal
    scaling does not certify positive definiteness or stability.

    Active intrinsic Float64Array views need current ordinary backing,
    pairwise disjoint conservative envelopes and stable exclusive
    synchronous lifetime. RAB current valid extents are supported;
    SAB, proxies, detached and OOB views are rejected. Pure JS callers
    guarantee hidden foreign physical nonaliasing. Native physical
    alias errors propagate and never trigger postmutation fallback.

    N=0 validates only active SCOND/AMAX and required scalar/main LDAB
    metadata, then writes SCOND=1, AMAX=+0. AB/S and inactive ndarray
    metadata are ignored. Only predispatch valid wider metadata uses
    JS fallback. Proposed Node>=16 is not compatibility proof; actual
    execution uses Node24/Linux.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string|number
        Row-major (101) or column-major (102).
    uplo: string|number
        Upper (121) or lower (122).
    N: integer
        Matrix order in [0,2147483646].
    KD: integer
        Bandwidth in [0,2147483646].
    AB: Float64Array
        Read-only full (KD+1)-by-N compact band view.
    LDAB: integer
        >=KD+1 column-major or >=max(1,N) row-major.
    S: Float64Array
        Output-only N-vector.
    SCOND: Float64Array
        Mutable scalar at index zero; retained on failure.
    AMAX: Float64Array
        Mutable maximum scalar at index zero.

    Returns
    -------
    info: number
        Zero or the first one-based nonpositive diagonal.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 4, 16, 64 ] );
    > var S = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 3 );
    > var C = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 1 );
    > var M = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 1 );
    > {{alias}}( 'column-major', 'lower', 3, 0, A, 1, S, C, M )
    0
    > S
    <Float64Array>[ 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 ]
    > C
    <Float64Array>[ 0.25 ]
    > M
    <Float64Array>[ 64 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( uplo, N, KD, AB, r, c, o, S, ss, os, SCOND, oc, AMAX, om )
    Uses signed element indexing AB[o+b*r+j*c], S[os+j*ss],
    SCOND[oc], AMAX[om] relative to the intrinsic typed-array views.
    Active offsets are nonnegative safe integers; full views fit and
    are injective with exact products/corners/byte sums. Used zero
    strides and overlapping conservative envelopes are rejected.
    On N=0 only active scalars and their offsets are inspected.

    Parameters
    ----------
    uplo: string|number
        Upper (121) or lower (122).
    N: integer
        Matrix order in [0,2147483646].
    KD: integer
        Bandwidth in [0,2147483646].
    AB: Float64Array
        Read-only full compact band view.
    r: integer
        Band-row element stride.
    c: integer
        Matrix-column element stride.
    o: integer
        Band starting offset.
    S: Float64Array
        Output-only N-vector.
    ss: integer
        Scaling element stride.
    os: integer
        Scaling starting offset.
    SCOND: Float64Array
        Mutable scalar; retained on failure.
    oc: integer
        Active SCOND offset.
    AMAX: Float64Array
        Mutable maximum scalar.
    om: integer
        Active AMAX offset.

    Returns
    -------
    info: number
        Zero or first one-based nonpositive diagonal.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 4, -0, 16, 25 ] );
    > var S = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 4 );
    > var C = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ -7 ] );
    > var M = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 1 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'lower', 4, 0, A, 1, 1, 0, S, 1, 0, C, 0, M, 0 )
    2
    > S
    <Float64Array>[ 4, -0, 16, 25 ]
    > C
    <Float64Array>[ -7 ]
    > M
    <Float64Array>[ 25 ]

    See Also
    --------
